flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your e-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: This is a recapture in the Queen's Gambit Exchange, not a free pawn. White's knight on c3 defends d5; I am restoring material, not winning it. Calling that 'undefended' trains me to misread every opening exchange.

flags.quote: Moving your g5-bishop to h4 is the strongest move because it saves your h4-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop is on g5. h6 asked it a question and it retreated. You named the destination as if a different bishop already lived on h4. I cannot tell which piece you mean, and you skipped the actual lesson: keep the pin rather than take on f6.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e7 with your h4-bishop puts it where the black queen can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been moving your h4-bishop to f2 because it saves your f2-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: I traded bishops. The eval drop is 69 centipawns, not a knight. Queen recapturing on e7 is the expected recapture, not me hanging a piece. Then Bf2 'saves your f2-bishop' — that bishop is on h4. Two lies in two sentences.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e7 with your queen is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: White just captured on e7 and the rook on e1 defends it. I recapture so I am not down a piece. 'Undefended' plus a wins-material reason on an equal trade is the same bug as ply 8, and I am starting to ignore you.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e4 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Yes, Qe7 was eyeing e3, but that is not why we played f3, Rae1, and Nge2 for ten moves. This is the thematic central break. Tell me I am opening the center after preparing it, not that a pawn ran away from a queen.

flags.quote: Moving your h5-knight to f6 is a blunder, but taking the pawn on e4 with your d-pawn would be better because you can likely pin the knight to the rook and you take the defender of the white bishop.
flags.critique: A 216-centipawn blunder with empty reasons, then 'likely pin' as if you are guessing. The real idea is dxe4: it opens the e-file so my queen pins Ne2 to the rook, and it takes a defender of Bd3. Drop 'likely.' Show the line. This is the first moment the game breaks and you hedged.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but taking the pawn on e4 with your d-pawn puts it at risk of attack from the white e1-rook and c3-knight. A better move would have been moving your pawn to c5.
flags.critique: Last move you told me dxe4 was the fix. White played Ng3, the knight left the pin line, and now the same capture is an inaccuracy. You never said why the position changed. I am worse because I missed it a ply ago, not because taking on e4 is a new kind of sin.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e4 with your g3-knight is a blunder because the pawn was undefended. A better move would have been moving your g3-knight to f5 because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: Taking an undefended pawn is not a blunder. Recapturing here drops a piece after ...Nxe4 and the long-diagonal recapture chain. Nf5 hits the queen on e7, not 'likely a pawn.' You used the capture as praise for a 296-centipawn lemon.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c5 is a blunder, but taking the knight on e4 with your f6-knight would be better.
flags.critique: 338 centipawns and you will not tell me why. Nxe4 wins a piece because Bb7 and the queen make the recapture fail. I played c5 discovering onto the queen like a trick and you shrugged 'would be better.' That is not coaching; that is a SAN dump.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but taking the rook on e1 with your queen puts it at risk of attack from the white f1-rook. A better move would have been moving your queen to d6 because you can likely pin the knight to the queen.
flags.critique: My queen is sitting on a rook. That is not 'at risk.' That is Q for R unless the engine is counting the hanging knight on c5 as compensation. And Qd6 'likely pin the knight to the queen' — which pin? Speak like a person or don't bother.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c5 with your d7-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: The queen on c2 defends c5. You just taught me it was a passed pawn, then one ply later it is 'undefended' when I take it. Pick a story. If the engine still likes Nxc5, say the recapture on c5 works because of the rook, not that the pawn had no defenders.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your c-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the Exchange Queen's Gambit and you had hanging, doubled pawns, and backward pawn as reasons. I do not care about a one-ply doubled d-pawn. Teach the plan: fix Black's pawn on d5, open c, later minority attack or e4. Otherwise this is just 'took a pawn, strongest.'

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to e7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You just celebrated Bg5 pinning my knight to the queen. Be7 breaks that pin. Development is true and useless. If you can see a pin, you can see an unpin.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The reason list is backward_pawn. I am preparing Bb7. If your structure detector fired, hide it. A 1200 knows b6 means the bishop is coming; your copy does not.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Reason: backward_pawn. This supports e4. That is the whole White plan in this setup. You called the preparatory move 'strongest' and tagged it with a weakness I did not create on purpose.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to b1 is a mistake, but moving your bishop to f5 would be better.
flags.critique: My queen stepped off the c-file so the rook would stop x-raying it. You give me Bf5 with no because. If it is a mistake, tell me what Bf5 does — hits the rook, keeps the queen active — not a shrug.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to e4 is a mistake, but moving your bishop to h7 would be better because it forces the king to respond.
flags.critique: Checks force the king to respond. That is what check means. Why Bh7+? I need the attacking idea, not the dictionary.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e4 with your f-pawn is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: Bd5 defends e4. This is a recapture, and you also stuffed isolated-pawn, pawn-shield, and king-safer into the same move. I recaptured a defended knight and you told me I won material while making my king safer. Pick one true sentence.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Last move you taught the pin of b5 to the queen. a6 attacks that pinned pawn. You had 'hanging' in the reasons and still said nothing. This is the easiest lesson in the game and you whiffed it.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to b2 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The queen steps off the a-file so a2 is no longer pinned to it. Your reason is ignored_threat, which sounds like I missed something, while the copy says strongest. I unpinned. Say that.

flags.quote: Moving your rook to c1 gives the opponent more access to your king. A better move would have been taking the rook on a2 with your rook because you skewer the black a5-rook, exposing the black pawn and then fork the black king and the black a2-rook.
flags.critique: I left a hanging rook. That is not king safety. Rxa2 takes the rook; the mash-up 'skewer then fork the king and the a2-rook' is garbage once that rook is gone. 316 centipawns for missing a capture, and you lectured me about shelter.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to d5 is a mistake, but moving your a5-rook to b5 would be better because your rook can use an open file.
flags.critique: Rb5 attacks the queen on b8. I do not need a lecture on open files. You had a tactic and you picked the phrase-bank line for 'rook likes files.'

flags.quote: Moving your a2-rook to g2 is the strongest move because it puts the opponent in check.
flags.critique: It is a check because it is a check. After g3 I am crashing through on g2 and building a mate net. 'That's the one' plus tautology is how you teach me to skip the coach panel.

flags.quote: Moving your a5-rook to a2 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Doubling on the second rank with mate ideas. Empty reasons. If you can see a skewer two moves ago, you can see two rooks on the same rank.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your rook to c8 lets black force checkmate in 9 moves. This lets black force checkmate in 9 moves. A better move would have been moving your rook to c5 because you can likely take a rook.
flags.critique: You said the mate sentence twice. Then the move that avoids mate is 'likely take a rook,' which is a hedge on the only thing that matters. I blundered into mate; do not weasel the save, and do not stutter.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures undefended wins
suggestions.detail: wins_material currently becomes 'the piece was undefended' when SEE is roughly a full piece. Equal recaptures (exd5, Qxe7, fxe4, Nxc5 on a queen-defended pawn) all fire it. Gate wins_material unless net SEE stays positive after a recapture on the same square, or if the captured unit was just the opponent's last mover and was defended. A 1200 notices immediately that opening trades are not free pieces.

suggestions.title: Do not praise the blunder's capture
suggestions.detail: Ply 33 attaches wins_material/capture/saves_piece to a 296cp blunder, so the because-clause says the pawn was undefended. select-insight should not feed constructive tactics of the played move into the verdict when classification is mistake/blunder. Use problem/consequence (hanging after recapture, piece-loss line) and put tactics on the suggested move only.

suggestions.title: Name hanging queens and rooks
suggestions.detail: hangingLossCopy returns null when |SEE| > 400, so Qxe1 becomes 'puts it at risk of attack from the rook' instead of 'you lose a queen.' Flip the cap: 150–220 exchange, then use the hanging unit's type (or materialLabel) all the way through queen. Silent 'at risk' should be for unclear SEE, not for a rook taking a queen.

suggestions.title: Name saved pieces from the from-square
suggestions.detail: saves_piece is labeled with the destination (h4-bishop, f2-bishop) so retreats read as saving a piece that is not there yet. Point NamedUnit.square at the origin, or describe 'your bishop' when same-type count is 1. Hits Bh4, Bf2, and every retreat in the corpus.

suggestions.title: Drop 'likely' on the engine move
suggestions.detail: capture/pin/fork with likely:true render as 'you can likely take a pawn/pin the knight.' On suggestedMoveSan that is the PV, the tactic either exists on the resulting board or it should not be emitted. Prefer fork targets actually attacked (Nf5 vs Qe7) over a generic pawn. Keep 'likely' only for follow-ups deeper than the fact layer can see.

suggestions.title: Stop calling bishops knights
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 250–399cp to 'a knight' and 200–249 to 'a bishop,' so a bishop trade on e7 becomes 'you lose a knight' on a 69cp inaccuracy. Use the hanging piece's type when known; otherwise say 'a minor piece' for 250–350. Never map a recapture SEE onto a different piece name.

suggestions.title: Do not print mate twice
suggestions.detail: allows_mate is both the problem ('lets black force checkmate in 9 moves') and the consequence ('this lets black force checkmate in 9 moves'). containsIgnoreCase only compares 24 characters, so the 'this ' prefix breaks the dedupe. Treat allows_mate as a single clause, or compare a normalized mate-in-N key instead of a prefix slice.

suggestions.title: Never ship a mistake with no why
suggestions.detail: missed_improvement with only a SAN (c5 vs Nxe4, Qb1 vs Bf5, b4 vs b3) is the worst empty copy in this game. If the suggested move has no because, pull fork/pin/hanging/check off the suggested position before falling back to open_file or king_more_exposed. Also suppress backward_pawn/center_control when a pin-exploit, unpin, or prepared pawn break is on the board (a6 vs pinned b5, f3/e4, Be7 vs Bg5).

whatWorked: Bg5: pin the knight to the queen — first sentence in the game that taught a real idea.
Nh5: discovered attack from the bishop onto Bh4. Concrete and true.
Nxc5: fork bishop and knight plus rook discovery on the queen. Best line in the dump.
dxc5 as a passed pawn, then Rb8 pinning b5 to the queen — structure and tactic both landed.

Ra4: pin a2 to the queen and discover the bishop. Rxa2 as a skewer on the second rank. Qb8+ as a discovered attack on the a2-rook. Qb1+ as a king-and-rook fork. When the tactic detector is sure, the copy is suddenly human.
